properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The delivery question behind Anthony's 2026-09-22 ask, separated from WHAT the standard is because a correct standard introduced badly is switched off within a week.

THE CLIFF, measured 2026-09-22: 47 of 288 capabilities have no passing check; 282 of 312 checks have no executable form; 448 of 598 artifacts have never been confirmed against what they realize. Any gate phrased as "a change touching something with no check fails the build" goes red immediately on ground that predates the rule.

⭐ THIS PROJECT HAS SOLVED IT TWICE AND WROTE DOWN WHY. The vocabulary-reach gate: "A REGRESSION GATE, NOT A CLEANLINESS GATE: it fails when a property becomes unreachable that the committed baseline does not already carry, and the 48 known ones are grandfathered rather than approved. A gate that goes red on day one over a long-standing state is a gate somebody switches off." The intent-authority gate did the same, and its boundary lives in the GRAPH — on a Decision — rather than in the script, so silencing a finding means editing the design where a review sees it.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) GRANDFATHER AND RATCHET, the established pattern. Commit a baseline of what is uncovered today; the gate fails only when that set GROWS. The baseline may shrink and never grow. ⭐ Proven twice here, and the boundary belongs in the graph rather than in the script. ⚠️ Counter: a baseline of 282 can sit untouched forever while the build stays green — it stops the bleeding and fixes nothing.

(b) RATCHET PLUS A DECLINING BUDGET. As (a), but the baseline must shrink by an agreed amount per release, so the debt has a schedule rather than a promise. ⚠️ Counter: an arbitrary rate becomes a thing to game or to quietly miss; it needs somebody to actually hold it.

(c) FREEZE AND CLEAR. Take Anthony's words literally — no further development until the 282 are triaged. Strongest signal, and it is what he said. ⚠️ Counter: weeks of no feature work, and this project has watched a large manual sweep go stale before; the honest version needs the work sized first, which nobody has done.

(d) SCOPE THE STANDARD NARROWLY FIRST. Apply it only to capabilities that are `realized` AND consumer-reachable — the surface other projects actually touch — and widen later. Far fewer than 288, and it targets the part where a regression costs somebody else. ⚠️ Counter: it needs "consumer-reachable" to be answerable, which `check_consumer_reach.py` partly does already.

⚠️ AND THE HONEST WARNING FROM THIS DESIGN'S OWN RECORD, which applies to every option: attaching a passing check to silence a finding is the failure mode — "a graph node green-washes exactly like a document", proved on a fleet where nine directory artifacts swallowed 373 files while the check read green. Whatever arrives, it must be possible for the number to GO DOWN.

📌 THE RULE THIS DELIVERS IS NOT YET RECORDED. Anthony stated it on 2026-09-22 — every change to the implemented design carries a test and regression cover — and chose STOP THE BUILD when asked what breaking it should cost. Writing it was interrupted by his question about how much of reflow2 is untested, which produced the measurement above and may change the answer. The rule is his and is still unwritten; this node is the delivery question it will need whenever it lands.
properties.name: OPEN — how does the new testing standard ARRIVE? 47 capabilities and 448 artifacts are already uncovered, so a gate that fires on existing ground goes red on day one and gets switched off
properties.rationale: Recorded as its own question because the standard and its arrival have different failure modes: a weak standard fails by being useless, and a strong standard introduced as a day-one cliff fails by being switched off — and the second failure leaves the project believing it has a rule it no longer has. Option (a) is not a recommendation so much as an observation that this repository has already chosen it twice under the same pressure and written down why.
